In ancient Hindu scriptures, Indra is depicted as the god of rain and thunder, the wielder of the Vajra or thunderbolt, and the giver of life-giving rains. The name Aranab is a reminder of the power of nature, the cycles of life and death, and the sacred bond between humans and the natural world. It is a name that evokes a sense of reverence and respect for the god Indra, and the role he plays in our lives.

Indra is not just a god of rain and thunder, but also a god of power, strength, and protection.
